From: Sophia Huang <sophia@orilabs.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year prepay — amortization / unused credit handling / ramp smoothing

Jonas,

Thanks for taking the intro call earlier. Orilabs is evaluating a 24–36 month prepay window to lock predictable unit costs for our LLM inference spend. A few asks we want to model and get firm pricing on before we escalate to procurement: 

- We want prepay to be amortized across the term (monthly allocation of purchased credits) rather than front-loaded consumption.
- A smoothing mechanism: our usage will ramp (Q1 conservative, Q3 heavy). We need to avoid cliff overages in year 1 while preserving unit economics for both parties.
- Discount tiers: what % do you offer for 2yr vs 3yr upfront prepay? Any differences if we include a nominal commitment to a baseline GPU capacity?
- Treatment of unused credits at annual true-ups: can we roll forward a portion vs a refund?

Attached is a high-level expected usage profile and some sample monthly forecasts. Can you send a working model and a short SOW/Draft term sheet we can share with finance? Ideally we want to lock language on true-up cadence and carryover caps.

Sophia
Sophia Huang
Head of Platform, Orilabs
Attachments: Orilabs_usage_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Huang <sophia@orilabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year prepay — amortization / unused credit handling / ramp smoothing

Sophia — thanks for the clear asks and the forecast. I put together an initial approach and attached a quick model (Orilabs_MultiYear_Modeling.xlsx) so you can tweak inputs. Summary proposal below: 

- Amortization: we allocate prepaid credits evenly across the months in the term. Monthly consumption draws from the amortized pool; overages bill at on-demand.
- Smoothing / ramp: propose a soft floor for year 1 equal to 60% of your 12-month baseline (so you won't hit large on-demand bills during expected ramp). Any usage below the floor accrues toward the amortized pool (i.e., we do not accelerate refunds).
- Discounting: 2-year prepay: 12% off list unit price; 3-year prepay: 18% off list. Discounts apply to base token/embedding rates only; overage on-demand rates are 50% above prepay unit price.
- True-up / carryover: annual true-up with up to 25% of the unused amortized credits eligible to roll forward to the next year (cap is percentage of the amount paid that year). Anything above that converts to one-time credit at 40% of list (i.e., partial cashable credit) or we can discuss a partial refund for enterprise procurement.

Next steps: if that direction looks reasonable I can loop in Marcus (legal/enterprise terms) and Kimberly (pricing/finance) to finalize margin guardrails and SOW language. I attached the modeling file and a one-page outline.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Team / Sophia — reviewed the numbers and legal guardrails. High level: we can proceed with the amortized + smoothing structure with the following adjustments to protect Redwood while remaining competitive for Orilabs: 

1) Discounts: approve 12% for 24-month prepay, 17% for 36-month prepay (we'll offer the 17% in exchange for a 12-month minimum commitment to baseline capacity and a one-time onboarding invoice).
2) Carryover cap: reduce to 20% roll-forward of unused amortized credits per contract year (any excess converts to a one-time account credit at 35% of list or is forfeited if contract terminated for cause).
3) True-up cadence: two checkpoints — 6 months (informal reconciliation) and annual formal true-up. Any shortfall after the formal true-up is invoiced at the contracted prepay unit price.
4) Termination: pro-rata refund only for unconsumed prepaid amounts beyond the allowed carryover cap, subject to standard clawback for discounts.

I've attached an updated SOW draft that includes the carryover cap, true-up schedule, and termination language. Sophia — if this aligns with Orilabs' procurement needs, let's schedule a 30-minute call to finalize the SOW and attach the model. Proposed times: Wed 6/23 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 6/24 14:00–14:30 PT.

Marcus Lin
